root_idea.summary: The root centers on blackness as the opposite of whiteness, with extensions to visible form, collective presence, secrecy, and eminence or leadership.
root_idea.development: From the color contrast of blackness, the lexicon extends to a person or body seen from a distance, a large collective body, secret speech through bringing persons close, and leadership understood through the people gathered around a chief. These extensions coexist with specialized color, landscape, bodily, and idiomatic usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: This is the plural adjective سُودٌ and is presented under the singular citation form أَسْوَد.

senses.definition: To become black or intensely black.
senses.usage_conditions: Form IX intransitive change-of-state usage; the Quranic verb describes faces becoming black.

senses.definition: Of a face, to become darkened with grief, shame, displeasure, or distress.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative Quranic facial expression, contrasted with the whitening of faces; it need not describe a literal change of physical color.

senses.definition: Black; having the color opposed to white.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular adjective أَسْوَد and its Quran-attested plural سُودٌ; the Quranic occurrences describe a black or intensely dark color.

senses.definition: Blackened or darkened; in particular, having a face marked by grief or displeasure.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participial form of the Form IX change of state; the Quranic contexts use it of a face whose dark appearance expresses distress.
A feminine resultative/passive-participial adjective; in the Quran it describes faces blackened as a condition of disgrace or distress.

senses.definition: A person of eminence, nobility, or high standing; a noble person.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic usage in وَسَيِّدًا presents the word as a quality of personal excellence or rank.

senses.definition: A husband or master of a household.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic narrative, the husband of the woman who attempts to restrain Joseph is called her سَيِّد; this is a relational household usage, not merely a general honorific.

senses.definition: A leader, chief, or ruler whose authority is followed.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural سَادَة in the Quran denotes the leaders or authorities whom people obey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become a chief, lord, master, or person of glory and eminence; to rule or hold dominion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic Form I verbal usage, including being the chief of one's people and exercising authority over another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave other camels or beasts behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form I usage said of a she-camel surpassing the other riding animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause or contract a disease called السُّوَاد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized health usage: of water, to cause the disease; of a person or animal, to be afflicted by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone a chief or master.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative usage, especially of a people appointing or treating someone as their leader.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slay; specifically, to slay chiefs or nobles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II usage and verbal noun referring to the killing of leaders.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boldness, daring, or courage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical interpretation of the Form II verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To void excrement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported Form II lexical interpretation; the source records disagreement over this sense and the sense of boldness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To blacken something or change its whiteness to blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive Form II color-change usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a face expressive of grief or displeasure; by extension, to grieve, displease, or disgrace someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of literal blackening, opposed to making the face white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write a rough first draft or original copy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage described as probably post-classical and contrasted with fair-copying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply beaten, worn hair-cloth as a remedy to sores or galls on camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized, figurative Form II expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a guest something that allays hunger before the morning meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or contend with another for superiority, including superiority in rank or in blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III reciprocal usage; the object of comparison may be social eminence or color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To meet someone in the blackness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction using blackness as the setting of the meeting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak secretly with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is explained through bringing one's person close to the other person's; the verbal nouns include سِوَاد and مُسَاوَدَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To entice toward sexual intercourse, or sexual intercourse itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the expression قُرْبُ الوِسَادِ وَطُولُ السِّوَادِ; it is distinct from the ordinary sense of secret speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act deceitfully or guilefully; to entice or turn someone by blandishment or deceptive arts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form III usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive away a lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative usage reported of the Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to labor at short or scant herbage with their lips without being able to master it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage said of camels working at insufficient vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beget or have born to one a black child, or a child who will be a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV usage with reported alternatives concerning color and status.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become married and master of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V reflexive/inchoative usage linking marriage with household authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slay or take captive a chief or noble person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported Form VIII usages of the expression اِسْتَادُوا بَنِي فُلَانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek marriage with, or marry among, noble or chief women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII usage with a person or group as the source of the sought marriage alliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough, black or black-stone tract at the foot or base of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A landscape noun for a narrow strip or portion of ground, often associated with a mountain containing a mine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land in which palm trees grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized landscape usage opposed to بَيْضَةٌ, according to the cited lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Chiefdom, lordship, mastery, glory, honor, dignity, eminence, or nobility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun derived from سَادَ and synonymous with the corresponding verbal nouns of leadership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small bird, especially a grape- and date-eating passerine bird with a long tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bird name with variant forms; the cited descriptions differ in how narrowly the bird is identified.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blackness; the color opposed to whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary noun of color, also used for the blackness of night or of particular parts of an animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart's core, inner part, heart's blood, or central clot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily and figurative expression for the innermost part of the heart or the innermost place of affection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The liver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A visible person, bodily form, or object seen from a distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The extension is explained by the dark appearance of a distant form; it applies to people and other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Household goods, utensils, baggage, equipment, or the collective matériel of an army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extension from a collection of visible bodily forms to the equipment and train gathered together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property, cattle, or a large amount of possessions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective-property usage, sometimes specifically meaning much property or livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collection, company, collective body, commonalty, majority, or great number.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote a group of people, the general body of a community, or a large number of things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collection of palm trees or other trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage based on the dark or green appearance of dense vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cultivated rural district surrounding towns and villages; especially the agricultural district of Iraq.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional landscape term for cultivated land and its settlements, named from the dark or green appearance of its trees and produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Secret speech with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun associated with سَاوَدَ; the lexicographical tradition distinguishes its vocalization and derivational analysis from سِوَادٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease affecting sheep or goats, or a human disease involving the liver; also a discoloration associated with drinking salt water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized medical and veterinary noun with several reported manifestations, including complexion and nail changes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An owner or proprietor, including the master or owner of a slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader possessive or household relation than the Quranic uses of noble person, husband, and leaders.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person distinguished by generosity, clemency, forbearance, self-restraint, piety, or useful excellence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are character-based extensions of the status term and are not limited to formal political leadership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A descendant of the Prophet, in a later specialized usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A present-day application recorded as distinct from the older general senses of chief, master, and noble person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief of the jinn or of another nonhuman group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A poetic or reported application of the leadership noun to jinn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The male leader or dominant one of a female wild-ass group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological application of the leadership term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mature or large he-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported with differing age specifications, including the third year, and can also be applied to camels and cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most eminent, exalted, or noble example of a thing; a paragon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extension from a person of eminence to any thing of outstanding rank, including the expression “paragon of speech.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive or epithet, reported especially in negative phrases such as “not a drop of water.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed anatomical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-known variety of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional food term associated with the Sawād of Iraq and Basrah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salt tracts containing or associated with a grass or plant of the najīl kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized landscape and botanical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greater or greatest in rank, estimation, dignity, generosity, or clemency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anomalous comparative or superlative usage distinct from the ordinary color adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Green or greenish when its appearance from a distance resembles blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional color extension explicitly based on the visual resemblance of green to black at a distance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Black people or a people characterized by blackness; by extension, the land of such people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or substantivized use of the color adjective, including the regional designation بلاد السودان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Black bile, one of the four bodily humors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical medical substantive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Arab race, in a contrastive classification opposed to أَحْمَرُ; according to some, the black race in that contrast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported ethnological use with disagreement over the referent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great, black, highly dangerous serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: When substantivized, the word denotes a particular venomous serpent rather than merely a black-colored animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The serpent and the scorpion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional dual expression named through predominance of the serpent's blackness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dates and water; in alternative reports, water and milk or water and a food plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional dual expression whose members and interpretation vary among authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A black stony tract and the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same dual expression, based on the blackness of both things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enemy, literally “black-livered.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative fixed expression; its plural denotes enemies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or emaciated sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression describing their condition, not a literal color classification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lucky arrow, especially one smeared with blood or regarded as a successful divining arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression associated with striking its target and seeking good fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bad word or a good word; by extension, a single word of any kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression in which black and white stand for opposed kinds of speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A footprint or footstep that is becoming effaced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional contrast with a fresh footprint called حَمْرَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cultivated or planted land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative landscape term opposed to uncultivated or “white” land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A very severe year, marked by hardship or scarcity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional scale of severe years in which black denotes a severity greater than the terms contrasted with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The black seed, identified especially with شُونِيز, nigella.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional medicinal designation; some authorities alternatively interpret it as a green herb because black and green can overlap in this lexicon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exceedingly or intensely black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anomalous emphatic epithet, as in “blacker than the blackness of the raven.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blackish or approaching black in color.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective formed from a diminutive of أَسْوَدُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or hide used for clarified butter or honey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized vessel or container term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One over whom rule or dominion is exercised; a subject of a master.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive relational adjective associated with سَيِّد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who gives birth to black children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine active participle of the Form IV usage أَسَادَ / أَسْوَدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water that causes the disease called السُّوَاد in those who drink it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized attributive construction concerning harmful water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough first draft or original copy of a book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage explicitly described as probably post-classical and contrasted with a fair copy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Guts containing blood drawn from a bound she-camel, roasted and eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized culinary-anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The partisans of the Abbasid dynasty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A historical collective designation based on their wearing black clothing.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Black clothing is a direct application of blackness.
Bird sense is grouped with the independently described bird entry.
Pointer to an earlier adjective discussion.
Participial pointer to the disease usage under سَادَ.

cautions: Some Lane Quran references use historical Roman-numeral citation conventions and are not converted here into modern verse locations unless the QAC location independently confirms the identification.
The QAC group سُودٌ is a plural adjective and is therefore accounted for under the singular public citation form أَسْوَد.
